textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 social-science · Understanding the Weather · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: Weather is the state of the atmosphere at a place at a given time: how hot or cold, wet or dry, windy or calm it is. It can change in a day. The atmosphere is the layer of air around the Earth.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Weather is the state of the atmosphere at a place at a given time: how hot or cold, wet or dry, windy or calm it is. It can change in a day. The atmosphere is the layer of air around the Earth.
beats.speakEn: Weather is the state of the atmosphere at a place at a given time: how hot or cold, wet or dry, windy or calm it is. It can change in a day. The atmosphere is the layer of air around the Earth.

beats.en: The elements of weather are temperature, precipitation, atmospheric pressure, wind and humidity. Temperature is how hot or cold the air is.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 social-science · Understanding the Weather · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Temperature is measured with a thermometer, in degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit. A thermometer uses a coloured liquid that expands when the temperature rises.

beats.en: Temperature is measured with a thermometer, in degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit. A thermometer uses a coloured liquid that expands when the temperature rises. 15 degrees Celsius equals 59 degrees Fahrenheit.
beats.speakEn: Temperature is measured with a thermometer, in degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit. A thermometer uses a coloured liquid that expands when the temperature rises. 15 degrees Celsius equals 59 degrees Fahrenheit.

beats.en: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air above us. It is measured by a barometer. At the sea coast it is about 1013 millibars; it falls as we climb a mountain. Climbers get less oxygen and must acclimatise.
beats.speakEn: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air above us. It is measured by a barometer. At the sea coast it is about 1013 millibars; it falls as we climb a mountain. Climbers get less oxygen and must acclimatise.

type: Temperature is measured with a thermometer, in degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 social-science · Understanding the Weather · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: Humidity is the amount of water vapour present in the air. Relative humidity of 20 to 40 percent is dry weather, and 60 to 80 percent is humid weather. It is measured by a hygrometer.

beats.en: Let us review the key takeaway from Understanding the Weather: Humidity is the amount of water vapour present in the air. Relative humidity of 20 to 40 percent is dry weather, and 60 to 80 percent is humid weather. It is measured by a hygrometer.
